newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Royal Sun integration plans on target.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Royal Sun integration plans on target.

text.p: Royal & Sun Alliance said on Thursday it was still on target to achieve annual cost savings of 175 million stg as it integrates operations following last year's six billion stg merger.

"The integration is progressing very well indeed, especially on the staffing front. The staff now know where they stand and the important thing is that we're continuing to retain business," Royal & Sun chief executive Richard Gamble told Reuters.
The 201 million pound charge for the integration of Royal Insurance and Sun Alliance Insurance was slightly higher than analyst expectations of between 150 and 175 million stg.
"It's just over one year's recovery which when you consider most companies work on a two year recovery cycle is very good," said Gamble.
The 175 million stg savings were very much a target figure but the company was always looking to reduce costs in other areas, he added.

Alongside integration costs, operating profits for Royal & Sun's first year were hit by 32 million stg related to currency movements and 167 million stg as the group changed the way it reserves for U.S. asbestos and environmental liabilities.

The quantification of future claims has moved to an individual site assessment and follows a similar move by B.A.T yesterday at its Eagle Star unit. Today's provision was intended to be the last for the U.S. claims based on current information.

The buy back of up to five percent of the group's shares resulted from the anticpation of having more capital than current business activities required and its desire to enhance shareholder value, said Gamble. "I can confidently say we're focused on shareholder value."
"After looking at the balance sheet we have decided the right thing is to return around five per cent of share capital to shareholders," said Gamble.

The group's experiences in both general and life insurance markets mirrored those of rivals who have reported in recent days with weather related losses in the U.S. increasing 36 million stg to 96 million stg.

"One has to say the largest factor in the results is the weather. General insurance is very competitive and rates are under pressure. In personal motor we are now seeing rates start to rise, in line with the claims experience, but everywhere else there is a lot of pressure on rates," said Gamble.
"Life business recovered quite dramatically and we are very conscious that any business we write these days must have a profit margin written into it." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
